CHIEF COMPLAINT
Suspected kidney stone with severe pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports severe pain that began 3 days ago in the left back, now radiating lower into the groin area. Pain is constant and she is unable to get comfortable. She is able to urinate and noted blood in urine this morning. She denies fever but reports chills and nausea. She is unable to eat due to pain severity. This is her third episode of kidney stones; previous episodes resolved in 3-4 days. She has taken Tylenol and ibuprofen without adequate relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No chest pain. No abdominal pain. Chills present. Nausea present. Hematuria noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension, Diabetes, Recurrent kidney stones (third episode), Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5 mg for hypertension, Metformin 500 mg for diabetes, Tylenol as needed, Ibuprofen as needed

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient enjoys French fries and has difficulty limiting salt intake. Admits to struggling with dietary modification.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure slightly elevated on presentation, attributed to pain. Heart: Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur. Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles or wheezes. Abdomen: Tenderness to palpation without rebound or guarding. CVA tenderness on right flank.

RESULTS
Home blood pressure readings: systolic 130s-150s, diastolic 70-80. Fasting blood glucose: low 100s. Previous A1C: 7.3. Glucose test from 2 months ago: 300.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Kidney stone with right-sided renal inflammation. Start Oxycodone 5 mg every 6-8 hours as needed for pain. Continue Tylenol for breakthrough pain. Increase fluid intake to promote stone passage. Provide urine strainer to monitor for stone passage. Referral to Urology for recurrent kidney stone management. Continue Norvasc 2.5 mg for hypertension. Continue Metformin 500 mg for diabetes. Referral to dietitian for dietary management.
